description: We’re a multidisciplinary team blending clinical medicine, biomedical data science, and AI/machine learning to build predictive astronaut health monitoring software for deep-space missions
summary: AEROVYNT is an onboard health co-pilot for astronauts on missions where Earth can’t answer in time. On a Mars trip, a radio message can take up to 22 minutes each way, so the crew has to make the first call on their own health. We built a working web app that learns each astronaut’s personal baseline instead of comparing them to Earth averages. It tracks 10 indicators, from sensors or a quick manual log, and shows them on a body map. It also tracks five NASA Human Research Program hazards, including radiation, isolation and distance from Earth. We checked it against NASA Inspiration4 lab data, real wearable data, and hundreds of simulated crews. The headline detection results are simulated, and we say so openly. It hasn’t had clinical review yet.
details: AEROVYNT learns each astronaut’s own baseline instead of judging them against Earth averages. They log 10 indicators, from onboard sensors or manually in a few seconds. A body map shows six physiological zones by status, and the app tracks five NASA Human Research Program hazards: radiation, isolation, altered gravity, distance from Earth and closed environments. It also has built-in checks for spaceflight eye changes (an Amsler grid) and blood clot red flags. We tested the engine on NASA Inspiration4 lab data, on real wearable data to calibrate sleep and heart rate noise, and on hundreds of simulated crews. We want to be upfront that the detection results are simulated.
